title: Naomi Stuchiner founded Beit Issie Shapiro in Ra’anana in memory of her father, for people with disabilities

trailer.text: Beit Issie Shapiro in Ra’anana is an Israeli nonprofit working to change the quality of life of people with disabilities and of their families.
The nonprofit was founded in memory of her father, Issie Shapiro, by Naomi Stuchiner, a recipient of the Israel Prize for lifetime achievement, who grew up in Johannesburg with her Orthodox parents.
Issie Shapiro, a recent immigrant from South Africa, died during a fundraising trip to the United States, and his children led the project after him.
In 1980 a small special education center for 16 children with complex cognitive disabilities opened in Ra’anana.
According to Sasha Weiss, the organization's work has since helped establish 180 early intervention centers across Israel.

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: Israel Prize for lifetime achievement for the founder; UN consultative status since 2012

paragraphs.text: Naomi Stuchiner grew up in Johannesburg with her Orthodox parents, Issie and Lucie Shapiro.
They taught her the importance of compassion backed by good deeds.
Her father led the establishment of the Selwin Segal Hostel, the first Jewish residential and care facility in South Africa for people with disabilities.
Stuchiner immigrated to Israel and worked as a social worker in a poor Tel Aviv neighborhood.
There she created the area's first daycare center for working mothers.
Issie Shapiro, too, was a recent immigrant from South Africa.
According to the Jewish Journal, he died of a heart attack a few weeks after setting out on a fundraising trip, and his family continued his dream.
His children led the project after his death on the trip to the United States.
According to the Jerusalem Post, in 1980, after her father's death, Naomi decided to establish the organization in his honor.
The organization was founded in his memory, continuing his path and his philosophy of life.
In 1980 Beit Issie Shapiro opened a small community-based special education center in Ra’anana.
The center opened for 16 children with complex cognitive disabilities.
According to the Jerusalem Post in 2006, the nonprofit initially provided a limited number of services.
Today the nonprofit's services are provided to children and adults with developmental disabilities.
These include moderate to severe intellectual developmental disability, autism and Down syndrome.
According to a 2006 article, the organization then offered 13 categories of programs and services, for children from six months to 12 years old.
According to the Beit Issie Shapiro website, in 1980 the organization opened a small community center for special education in Ra'anana.

stations.title: Starting early: one center, 180 centers and a law

paragraphs.text: According to Hanna Yamin-Cherki, children with disabilities in Israel typically attend separate early intervention centers.
According to her, their peers without disabilities go to regular daycare centers.
According to a 2006 article, the staff are proud of the Early Intervention Center, the first in Israel, which treats developmental problems at a young age.
According to the same article, many of the center's "graduates" went on to regular kindergartens and other mainstream educational programs.
According to Amir Lerner, a one-and-a-half-year-old girl who could not bear weight on her legs stood with assistance and smiled.
This happened within a few weeks of the start of a program that combined motor rehabilitation and emotional therapy.
Beit Issie also set up an Early Learning Center for Arab children in the nearby town of Kalansua.
According to Sasha Weiss, Beit Issie worked on drafting the Law of Early Intervention, which was passed in 2000.
The law grants every toddler with a disability access to early intervention daycares.
According to Sasha Weiss, the organization's work has helped establish 180 early intervention centers across Israel since its founding.
According to Lerner, the organization formed a coalition of about 60 bodies, parents, professionals and nonprofits, to advance legislation.
Among the laws it advanced: the Rehabilitative Daycare Centers Law, a law extending absence days for parents of children with disabilities, and laws in the field of accessibility.
According to Lerner, the organization has to date changed 15 substantive laws and regulations that grant new rights to thousands of families.

stations.title: A Snoezelen room and a dental clinic

paragraphs.text: According to the director, Jean Judes, the first Snoezelen room in Israel was built at Beit Issie.
According to her, the first research in the world on such a room was also conducted there.

The organization's page includes a thank-you letter for treatment that is "much more than 'a healthy mouth'," in which its writers describe a deep process of changing awareness and turning anxieties into small joys.

According to director Jean Judes, mealtimes are therapeutic time at the early intervention center, because children with severe disabilities have eating difficulties, including problems swallowing and a lack of sensation in the mouth, and so it is important to teach them to eat as independently as possible.
The dental clinic at Beit Issie Shapiro was established to provide quality care in the community to people with disabilities who cannot be treated at regular clinics.
According to a 2006 article, the clinic offered full dental care through more than 100 volunteer dentists and hygienists.
Today the staff includes 12 doctors, among them specialists in oral rehabilitation, orthodontics and general anesthesia.
The clinic operates under license and supervision of the Ministry of Health, and it is accessible and adapted.
Those who have difficulty financing treatment at the clinic receive assistance from the Beit Issie Shapiro family support fund.
According to Judes, in 2005 the organization gave out NIS 250,000 in scholarships, and no child is turned away for inability to pay.

stations.title: A school, and students who make their voices heard

paragraphs.text: The organization's special education school in Ra’anana serves children aged six to twelve with complex physical and intellectual disabilities.
According to the organization's website, Rhea, an 11-year-old girl with a cognitive disability, used Grid software, which pairs symbols with words.
This allowed her to express herself and engage in literacy.
The Young Leadership Group is a group of about ten high school students with physical and cognitive disabilities that meets weekly in Ra’anana.
It is one of the leadership center's five groups.
Gadi Rothschild, 16, attended the Beit Issie Early Intervention Center until age 3 and has taken part in the group since middle school.
According to the Central Bureau of Statistics, in 2022 approximately one in nine residents of Israel was recognized as a person with a disability requiring accessibility accommodations.
The teenagers in the group said that clear instructions for people with hearing or sight impairments are lacking.
They also said that accessible shelters are lacking and that there is no clear marking of the accessible shelters.
The group planned and ran a public awareness campaign on shelter accessibility, which ran on social media and on Channel 12.
The Beit Raz campus is named after Raz Fisher, a former Beit Issie child who died at age 4.
Tamar Fisher, Raz's mother, said that the parents came to the project because they felt a responsibility to give new parents a place of hope.
According to Maariv, the campus was established in partnership with the Buksembaum Foundation, the Joint, the Ministry of Welfare and the Ministry of Education.

According to eJewishPhilanthropy, which reported on the campus inauguration in June 2025, the new campus was expected to take in 80 children in September of that year, 40 with disabilities and 40 without.
According to the Azrieli Foundation, at Beit Raz children with and without disabilities play and learn together.

According to Lerner, a recently completed pilot found that integrating children with and without disabilities in an inclusive daycare yields far greater benefits for all the children, their families and the community.
The campus also includes the Wohl Therapy Center and the new National Center for Emotional and Mental Health for people with disabilities and their families.
According to the Azrieli Foundation, this is the first national center of its kind in Israel, with therapy, trauma intervention and training of clinical psychology interns.
According to Lerner, the organization is receiving certification from the Ministry of Health to become a four-year residency center for clinical psychology.
Amir Lerner served in the Air Force as a navigator and has been CEO of Beit Issie Shapiro since 2020.
According to him, at the start of the war the organization worked with an evacuated community from Kiryat Shmona, including children on the spectrum.
When the war with Iran broke out, the organization opened a hotline for disability professionals, and the therapists stayed in personal contact with families.
According to Lerner, on the day the war broke out they contacted each of the families and patients, to make sure they were safe and to begin providing support.
According to him, the emotional distress of children and adults with disabilities is not always visible, but it is very deep.

stations.title: From Ra’anana to the world: numbers and recognition

paragraphs.text: According to Lerner, more than 90,000 professionals have received training at Beit Issie over the years.
According to him, 40% of the organization's budget comes from philanthropy, 30% from government support and 30% from self-generated income from sales of services.
According to a 2006 article, the center's reported income in 2004 was $6,622,500, from government grants, donors and training.
In 2012 the organization received special consultative status with the UN Economic and Social Council, and the UN turned to it for advice on inclusion.
According to Maariv, the organization is regarded as a model to emulate and has been included in UNESCO reports.

Friendship Park, established with the help of the organization Let All the Children Play, is Israel's first accessible and inclusive playground for children with and without disabilities, and serves as a model worldwide.
The president of Down Syndrome International commended the institution and asked that the organization also operate in India.
According to Lerner, Florida International University purchased from the organization the program "The Art of Living" for the inclusion of people with disabilities at the university.
According to the Azrieli Foundation, the organization trains professionals in Africa, Europe, and North and South America.
According to the organization's publication, it has partnerships with 30 countries.
The organization launched the $25,000 Shlomot Prize, recognizing excellence in emotional therapy for people with disabilities.
The Ministry of Education announced that the Israel Prize for lifetime achievement would be awarded to Naomi Stuchiner, the founder of Beit Issie Shapiro.
In 2020 the Jerusalem Post wrote that she had founded the organization almost 40 years earlier.

versions.says: A 2006 article: 16,000 people, locally, nationally and worldwide
Sasha Weiss: more than 500,000 people worldwide each year
Israel Prize committee (2020): more than half a million Israelis each year

claims.quote: The Beit Issie Young Leadership Group is a group of about 10 high-schoolers with a spectrum of physical and cognitive disabilities that meet weekly

claims.text: גדי רוטשילד בן ה-16 למד במרכז להתערבות מוקדמת של בית איזי עד גיל 3 ומשתתף בקבוצת ההנהגה הצעירה מאז חטיבת הביניים.
claims.quote: he attended the Beit Issie Early Intervention Center until he was 3.

claims.text: לפי הלשכה המרכזית לסטטיסטיקה, ב-2022 אחד מכל תשעה תושבים בישראל בקירוב מוכר כאדם עם מוגבלות הזקוק להתאמות נגישות.
claims.quote: one in nine Israeli residents (approximately) has been recognized by state institutions as a person with a disability

claims.text: בני נוער מקבוצת ההנהגה הצעירה סיפרו שחסרות הוראות ברורות לבעלי לקות שמיעה או ראייה, שחסרים מקלטים נגישים ושאין סימון ברור של המקלטים הנגישים.
claims.quote: not having instructions available clearly for those with hearing or sight impairments; a lack of bomb shelters with accessibility; and a lack of clear marking of designation

claims.text: הקבוצה תכננה והפעילה קמפיין מודעות ציבורי על נגישות מקלטים, שרץ ברשתות החברתיות ובערוץ 12.
claims.quote: plan, create and implement a full public-awareness campaign that ran on social media and National Israel television on Channel 12.

claims.text: קמפוס בית רז נקרא על שם רז פישר, ילד לשעבר בבית איזי שמת בגיל 4.
claims.quote: It is named after Raz Fisher, a former Beit Issie child who died when he was 4.

claims.text: תמר פישר, אמו של רז, אמרה שההורים הגיעו לפרויקט כי הרגישו אחריות לתת להורים חדשים מקום של תקווה.
claims.quote: We came to this project as parents because we felt we had a responsibility to give these new parents a place of hope.

claims.text: לפי מעריב, הקמפוס הוקם בשיתוף קרן בוקסמבאום, הג'וינט, משרד הרווחה ומשרד החינוך.
claims.quote: הקמפוס הוקם בשיתוף עם קרן בוקסמבאום, הג'וינט, משרד הרווחה ומשרד החינוך

claims.text: לפי eJewishPhilanthropy, בספטמבר יקלוט הקמפוס החדש 80 ילדים, 40 עם מוגבלות ו-40 בלעדיה, מגיל לידה עד 3.
claims.quote: the campus will welcome 80 children — 40 with and 40 without disabilities — from infants to age 3

claims.text: לפי קרן עזריאלי, בבית רז ילדים עם ובלי מוגבלות משחקים ולומדים יחד מגיל שישה חודשים.
claims.quote: Beit Raz sees children with and without disabilities playing and learning together, from the age of six months old.

claims.text: לפי לרנר, פיילוט שהושלם לאחרונה מצא ששילוב ילדים עם ובלי מוגבלות במעון משולב מניב תועלת גדולה בהרבה לכל הילדים, למשפחותיהם ולקהילה.
claims.quote: integrating children with and without disabilities in an inclusive daycare framework yields far greater benefits for all children, their families and the community.

claims.text: הקמפוס כולל גם את מרכז וואהל לטיפול ואת המרכז הלאומי החדש לבריאות הנפש והרגש לאנשים עם מוגבלויות ולמשפחותיהם.
claims.quote: The campus also includes the Wohl Therapy Center and Israel’s new National Center for Emotional and Mental Health for individuals with disabilities and their families.

claims.text: לפי קרן עזריאלי, בית איזי הקים את המרכז הלאומי הראשון בישראל לבריאות הנפש לאנשים עם מוגבלויות, עם טיפול, התערבות בטראומה והכשרת מתמחים בפסיכולוגיה קלינית.
claims.quote: Beit Issie has established Israel’s first National Mental Health Center for People with Disabilities

claims.text: לדברי לרנר, הארגון מקבל אישור ממשרד הבריאות להפוך למרכז התמחות בן ארבע שנים בפסיכולוגיה קלינית.
claims.quote: We’re receiving certification from the Ministry of Health to become a four-year residency center for clinical psychology.

claims.text: לרנר שירת בחיל האוויר כנווט ומשמש מנכ"ל בית איזי שפירא מאז 2020.
claims.quote: לרנר שירת בתפקיד נווט בטייסת הפנטומים. הוא משמש מנכ"ל בית איזי שפירא מאז 2020

claims.text: לדברי לרנר, הארגון עבד בתחילת המלחמה עם קהילה מקריית שמונה שפונתה, ובהם ילדים על הספקטרום.
claims.quote: we worked with a specific community from Kiryat Shmona, all of them with children on the spectrum who were all evacuated together

claims.text: עם פרוץ המלחמה עם איראן פתח הארגון קו חם לאנשי מקצוע בתחום המוגבלות, והמטפלים נשארו בקשר אישי עם משפחות.
claims.quote: Beit Issie opened a hotline for disabilities professionals to offer them support and guidance

claims.text: לדברי לרנר, ביום פרוץ המלחמה יצרו קשר עם כל אחת מהמשפחות והמטופלים כדי לוודא שהם בטוחים ולהתחיל לספק מענה.
claims.quote: ביום שפרצה המלחמה יצרנו קשר עם כל אחת מהמשפחות והמטופלים שלנו

claims.text: לדברי עמיר לרנר, המצוקה הרגשית של ילדים ומבוגרים עם מוגבלות לא תמיד נראית לעין אך היא עמוקה מאוד.
claims.quote: המצוקה הרגשית של ילדים ומבוגרים עם מוגבלות לא תמיד נראית לעין, אבל היא עמוקה מאוד

claims.text: לדברי לרנר, יותר מ-90,000 אנשי מקצוע עברו הכשרה בבית איזי לאורך השנים.
claims.quote: Over 90,000 professionals have passed through Beit Issie over the years, receiving training in fields that are relevant to rehabilitation

claims.text: לדברי לרנר, 40% מתקציב הארגון מגיעים מפילנתרופיה, 30% מתמיכה ממשלתית ו-30% מהכנסה עצמית ממכירת שירותים.
claims.quote: 40% comes from philanthropy, 30% from government support and the remaining 30% is self-generated through sales of services

claims.text: לפי מעריב, מודל ההכנסות של הארגון כולל 30% הכנסות ממשלתיות ו-30% הכנסות עצמיות מטיפולים, הכשרות ומחקר.
claims.quote: מודל עסקי מגוון ויציב: 30% הכנסות ממשלתיות, 30% הכנסות עצמיות (כגון טיפולים, הכשרות ומחקר)

claims.text: לפי כתבה משנת 2006, ההכנסה המדווחת של המרכז ב-2004 הייתה 6,622,500 דולר ממענקי ממשלה, תורמים והכשרות.
claims.quote: With a reported 2004 income of $6,622,500 from government subsidies, local and international donors, training and continuing education courses

claims.text: לפי מעריב, הארגון נחשב למודל לחיקוי ונכלל בדוחות של אונסק"ו.
claims.quote: הארגון נחשב כיום למודל לחיקוי ונכלל בדוחות יוקרתיים של אונסק"ו

claims.text: פארק חברים, שהוקם בעזרת ארגון Let All the Children Play, הוא המגרש המשחקים הנגיש והמשלב הראשון בישראל לילדים עם ובלי מוגבלות ומשמש מודל בעולם.
claims.quote: Friendship Park – Israel's first inclusive and accessible playground for children with and without disabilities, which serves as a model for similar projects worldwide

claims.text: נשיאת Down Syndrome International שיבחה את המוסד וביקשה שהארגון יפעל גם בהודו.
claims.quote: approached Maor to commend the institution on its work and expressed her interest that the organization come to her country, India

claims.text: לדברי לרנר, אוניברסיטת פלורידה הבינלאומית רכשה מהארגון את תוכנית "The Art of Living" לשילוב אנשים עם מוגבלות באוניברסיטה.
claims.quote: They’ve purchased a program from us called ‘The Art of Living.’ It supports the inclusion of people with disabilities within a university environment

claims.text: לפי קרן עזריאלי, הארגון פועל כמוקד משאבים עולמי ומכשיר אנשי מקצוע באפריקה, אירופה וצפון ודרום אמריקה.
claims.quote: training professionals across Africa, Europe, and North and South America

claims.text: לפי פרסום הארגון, יש לו שיתופי פעולה עם 30 מדינות.
claims.quote: מעגלי השפעה בארץ ובעולם | שיתופי פעולה עם 30 מדינות

claims.text: הארגון השיק את פרס שלומות בסך 25,000 דולר להוקרת מצוינות בטיפול רגשי לאנשים עם מוגבלות.
claims.quote: a $25,000 award recognizing excellence in emotional therapy for people with disabilities

claims.text: לפי כתבה משנת 2006, הארגון משפיע על 16,000 אנשים מקומית, ארצית ובעולם.
claims.quote: She has guided its evolution into a pace-setting facility that impacts 16,000 people locally, nationally, and worldwide.

claims.text: לדברי וייס, הארגון משפיע על יותר מ-500,000 איש בעולם מדי שנה.
claims.quote: the organization affects over 500,000 people worldwide each year, Weiss said.

claims.text: לפי ועדת פרס ישראל (2020), בית איזי שפירא משפיע לטובה על חייהם של יותר ממחצית המיליון ישראלים מדי שנה.
claims.quote: in less than 40 years, Issie Shapiro has become a center that positively influences the lives of over half a million Israelis every year.

claims.text: לפי מעריב, בית רז מאפשר שילוב חינוכי בגיל הרך לילדים עם וללא מוגבלות מגיל שנה עד 3.
claims.quote: ילדים עם וללא מוגבלות בגילֵי שנה עד 3 במודל חינוכי משולב

claims.text: לפי אתר בית איזי שפירא, ב-1980 פתח הארגון מרכז קהילתי קטן לחינוך מיוחד ברעננה.
claims.quote: In 1980, Beit Issie Shapiro launched a groundbreaking initiative in Israel by opening a small, community-based

quote_translations.c1: Beit Issie Shapiro is a nonprofit working to change the quality of life of people with disabilities and their families
quote_translations.c2: The organization was founded in memory of Issie Shapiro, of blessed memory, and in continuation of his path and his philosophy of life
quote_translations.c3: Children and adults with developmental disabilities, including moderate to severe intellectual developmental disability, autism, Down syndrome
quote_translations.c47: We formed a coalition of about 60 bodies – parents, professionals and nonprofits
quote_translations.c48: The Rehabilitative Daycare Centers Law, a law extending absence days for parents of children with disabilities, and laws in the field of accessibility
quote_translations.c46: To date we have changed 15 substantive laws and regulations – which grant new rights to thousands of families
quote_translations.c72: It is a deep process of change in awareness, turning anxieties into small joys and turning an unpleasant struggle, impassable as far as I was concerned, into a possible one
quote_translations.c21: To provide quality care in the community to people with various disabilities who cannot receive treatment at regular clinics
quote_translations.c22: The clinic staff includes 12 doctors, among them a specialist in dentistry for children and youth, a specialist in orthodontics, a specialist in oral rehabilitation
quote_translations.c23: The clinic operates under license and supervision of the Ministry of Health, and it is adapted and accessible in every respect
quote_translations.c73: Financial assistance is provided from the Beit Issie Shapiro family support fund
quote_translations.c43: The campus was established in partnership with the Buksembaum Foundation, the Joint, the Ministry of Welfare and the Ministry of Education
quote_translations.c71: Lerner served as a navigator in the Phantom squadron. He has served as CEO of Beit Issie Shapiro since 2020
quote_translations.c70: On the day the war broke out we contacted each of our families and patients
quote_translations.c18: The emotional distress of children and adults with disabilities is not always visible, but it is very deep
quote_translations.c74: A diverse and stable business model: 30% government income, 30% self-generated income (such as therapies, training and research)
quote_translations.c60: The organization is regarded today as a model to emulate and has been included in prestigious UNESCO reports
quote_translations.c64: Circles of influence in Israel and around the world | Partnerships with 30 countries
quote_translations.c68: Children with and without disabilities aged one to 3 in an inclusive educational model
